source_text: Diabolus enim creat - dicis - si ex hoc vulnere creantur, quod diabolus naturae, quae primum condita est, inflixit humanae: et damnantur nuptiae, si aliquid unde damnabiles generantur, habere creduntur: nec omnia peccata dimittuntur in Baptismo, si aliquod in baptizatis coniugibus remanet malum, ex quo generentur mali. Quemadmodum autem non est iniquus Deus, qui cum baptizatis remittat peccata propria, parvulum damnat, quia cum ab illo crearetur, nesciens nec volens etiam ex illis parentibus, quibus remissa fuerant, traxit aliena? Nec virtus, cui vitiositas intellegitur esse contraria, posse creditur perfici; quia ingenerata vitia incredibile est posse consumi: quae iam nec vitia deputanda sunt. Non enim peccat, qui non potest aliud esse quam creatus est Nos asserendo originale peccatum, diabolum dicere hominum nascentium conditorem, damnare nuptias, negare in Baptismo dimitti universa peccata, Deum crimine iniquitatis arguere, desperationem perfectionis ingerere
pass_a_gloss: The-devil for creat - you-say - if from this wound are-created, that/which the-devil of-nature, which first condita is, inflicted humanae: and are-condemned marriages, if something whence worthy-of-condemnation generantur, to-have they-believe: nor all-things sins are-dismissed in in-baptism, if aliquod in the-baptized spouses remanet evil, from whither generentur of-evil. just-as however not is unjust God, who when/with the-baptized remits sins own, little-one condemns, because when/with from illo was-being-created, not-knowing nor willing also from those parents, to-whom remissa fuerant, drew others'-things? nor virtue, to-whom viciousness to-be-understood to-be contrary, to-be-able believes to-be-perfected; because inborn faults incredibile is to-be-able to-be-destroyed: which already nor faults to-be-counted are. not for sins, who not is-able other to-be than/which created is we asserendo original sin, diabolum to-say of-human-beings nascentium founder, damnare marriages, to-deny in in-baptism dimitti all-things sins, God crimine of-iniquity arguere, desperationem perfectionis ingerere.

lemmas.lexica: LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself
LS nuptiae=nuptials; Blaise Christian marriage good
LS malum; Blaise malum naturale vs malum voluntatis

pass_b_english: The devil creates them, if they are created from the wound the devil inflicted on human nature as it was first made. Marriage is condemned if it is believed to contain something from which people deserving condemnation are born. Nor are all sins forgiven in baptism if some evil remains in baptized married couples, from which evil people are born. And how is God not unjust, if he forgives baptized people their own sins, yet condemns an infant because, when created by him, the infant unknowingly and unwillingly inherited other people’s sins—even from parents whose sins had been forgiven? Nor can virtue, whose opposite is understood to be vice, be thought capable of perfection: it is incredible that inborn faults could be destroyed. Indeed, these should no longer even be counted as faults. Someone who cannot be anything other than what they were created to be is not sinning.

choices.why: Julian's charge against Augustine: treating evil as a nature rather than as will.
Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.
Julian defends marriage as God's work against the charge that generation transmits sin.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
